clearly a massive internet sensation | i will do my best to try to cut through the hype and get to the core of the matter | undertale is an rpg based on games from the bit era snesgenesis with elements of bullet dodging games | the mechanics are fairly straightforward walk around and interact with characters occasionally getting into turn-based combat | the combat interface features option for attacking the monsters which uses a timing minigame running and using items | the innovation comes in the ability to perform a variety of actions toward monsters | choosing certain actions will convince the monster that you are friendly and can end an encounter without you or the monster dieing | this awards you with gold but does not award xp | when it is the monster's turn there is a brief dodging minigame | this gets tougher as the game progresses but the game is not a bullet hell | i've been okay even on my low lv run despite being pretty bad at bullet dodging | the graphics of undertale are mostly bit sprites and pretty well done | the game looks well put together but don't d graphics or photo realistic designs | the musical score for this game is one of the best i have heard in an indie game | it's a nice blend of bit retro tunes and a wide variety of musical styles ranging from symphonic to jazz to rock to polka | sound effects are otherwise fairly basic | each character has a particular sound effect for their voice making it possible to recognize them but there is almost no voice work in the game | undertale's hype is built almost entirely on its story | it has a large number of ending variations | every boss you kill or spare changes the outcome of the game | it is indeed possible to live up to the game's tagline of being the rpg where no one has to die and that is a very satisfying if challenging outcome | you can also kill every single monster in the game which is challenging for its own reasons | the game has a message to it but it is not preachy or really self-righteous about it | the game just treats monsters in random encounters like characters as opposed to being just a source of xp | it also takes into account game mechanics in the story saving and loading is something that happens in the world of the game | characters in undertale are highly memorable | toriel and flowey both of who show up in the first few moments of the game and are on the cover art are both very interesting characters with a solid amount of backstory available to explore | writing is clear and easy to read and the game's humor is pretty impressive | i have written this with the intent of not spoiling the game and it is best experienced unspoiled | i read spoilers beforehand and wish i hadn't if this sounds at all interesting to you i recommend buying undertale | it is well worth $ us the soundtrack is great and when it is on sale it's a steal |

review_text: obsidian studios has long had a talent for creating excellent sequels to hit rpgs crafted by top-notch studios and fallout: new vegas is no exception | created using the same engine as fallout new vegas is really more of a standalone title than a true sequel | whereas fallout transported the player to the ruins of d | c | on the east coast new vegas returns to the original setting that was developed back during the first two fallout games | only a few meager hints at what happened in fallout can be found in this game highlighting the utter lack of communication between the east coast and the west and enhancing the feel that these are separate worlds | new vegas borrows heavily from material that was developed for the original fallout which was canceled when black isle studios folded back in | fans of the original games will instantly feel a familiarity with the setting and factions featured in new vegas and there are many references to characters and events that took place in the first two games | there are a few stark differences between fallout: new vegas and its predecessor fallout | while i personally feel that fallout had a far more compelling story many of its gameplay elements could be problematic; on the other hand new vegas' story is not quite as good but its gameplay is much improved | new vegas reintroduces traits as a mechanic during character creation allowing you to give your new character bonuses in exchange for taking on certain penalties | the level cap with all dlc installed has been increased from a mere thirty to a whopping fifty levels and the number of available perks has gone through the roof; to balance this and prevent characters from being quite as overpowered as they could become in fallout perks are now only available every other level | that being said there are far more 'acquired' perks available many through dlc that a player can accumulate by repeatedly using specific weapon types or killing tons of foes | several skills have been eliminated or condensed into other skills and survival the ability to 'live off the land' by gathering and cooking plants and meats has been added | survival ties in directly with the new 'hardcore' game mode which requires the player to eat drink and sleep regularly in order to stay alive | the dearth of skill books found in fallout accounting for half of your total skill points if you could find all of them has been replaced with 'skill magazines' that provide a large temporary boost to a given skill once you read them | while the vats mechanic still remains fps players can now 'run and gun' much more effectively with the addition of a genuine 'iron sights' system that allows for direct los targeting | weapon modifications have also been re-introduced enabling the player to upgrade a 'vanilla' weapon into something more powerful | the number of weapons and ammo types available has shot up dramatically; each weapon uses rounds of a specific caliber or gauge and most ammo even those used for energy weapons has subtypes with varying effects allowing you to switch out your rounds to deal more damage stun or successfully injure heavily armored foes | crafting has been made far more comprehensive than in fallout and the inclusion of ammo benches allows players to recycle spent rounds as well as convert bullets that they don't use into types that they fire more frequently | with four dlc packs that add entirely new areas off of the main map new vegas' world is considerably larger and more complex than that of fallout | while new vegas lacks much of the thematic punch that helped the player relate to fallout 's main character it results in the courier feeling much more like a blank slate that the player can imbue with whatever qualities and history they prefer | combined with traits the inclusion of the survival skill hardcore mode and a far more diverse and open world new vegas offers far greater opportunities for genuine roleplaying than fallout did | even more so than in fallout the player can choose to ignore the main quest completely if they wish turning the mojave wasteland into a figurative and literal sandbox | there are so many different factions locations and sidequests available that a player could sink a hundred hours in and still not experience everything that fallout: new vegas has to offer |

review_text: bioshock infinite is at once a game you've never seen before and something you instinctually have done many times in the past | there is a grand sense of wonder and beauty when you explore the world; a flying city with sweeping vistas and elevators placed in strategic places to show them off perfectly | from the bizarre new tech on show at the fair to the cargo being hoisted into the clouds by a pair of overhead rails; this is not a place you have explored before | and at the same time you feel at home here | you know to search every garbage can and barrel for loot; that you can 'hack' the vending machines and that a lightning bolt plus a shotgun make for a great one-two combo | so is that it; is this just rapture in the sky | thankfully no | while thematically similar the game forges its own path with a bold story and some very interesting characters | of course the star of the show is your new ai teammate elizabeth | you could say the elizabethbooker dynamic steals the show causing most of the secondary characters to feel much more minor than they could have if you were adventuring alone | however this is not a bad thing | much like the alyx sections of half life having a great companion with you can make the journey that much more interesting | and while she won't be sniping zombies for you elizabeth definitely pulls her weight in combat by tossing you supplies and warping in everything from rpgs to automated turrets | the story itself explores many themes from racism and slavery to religious zealotry and even a good dose of sci-fi reality bending | without wanting to go into spoilers lets just say the story is something that will keep you interested and is the major reason this game is a success | even the ending is satisfying and may have you head right onto the internet to discuss it with others | there were a few parts of the game that i didn't care for as much as others; the main ones being design choices for combat | i have never been a fan of the ' guns' idea for shooters | when this is in place i never bother experimenting with new guns | i played really well with the sniper rifle and the rpgvolley gun and because this combo was working; i would say i didn't even bother with about % of the guns in game | sure; the hand cannon looked interesting but if i take it i have to drop one of my 'main' guns and what if i don't like it | the other was the inability to store a few salts bottles mana potions in some kind of inventory | i found that while useful vigors were only useable in the first third of any large battle | once you run out of salts you have to switch to guns only unless elizabeth happens to toss you some | if i can carry extra rpg rounds or extra sniper bullets why can i not carry a few extra vigors recharges | on the topic of vigors; they do seem a little out-of-place in this world | in the first bioshock plasmids were the driving force of the game | they were the reason the city was in ruins and that lunatics would leap at you with their hook-hands | in columbia they just seem to be a novelty item found at fairs and bars in ice cream shops or just sitting out in the open in a crate | the fact that they have no impact on the world and are not even widely used by the citizens besides a few select elite soldiers feels a bit odd | their inclusion feels like it was done because this is a 'bioshock' title and you can't have bioshock without zappy-hands | at the end of the day however these issues do little to derail what ends up being an amazing game | the story and the gameplay are both top-notch and the game will likely have you enthralled in it's experience for the hours it takes you to complete it |

review_text: originally posted on my blog [hlilje | tumblr | com] bioshock has always had a special place in my heart a game set in a wonderful world plagued by underwhelming gameplay | bioshock improved slightly upon the mechanics but did nothing to evolve the setting itself which resulted in an experience a bit too familiar | bioshock infinite thus resembles the first titles in the series by creating an amazing world with rather average gameplay and gunplay which through the environment alone still manages to keep you interested in it | the opening level takes you the former pinkerton booker dewitt on a boat trip to a lighthouse with a simple mission: > bring us the girl and wipe away the debt | shortly thereafter you are taken to columbia the utopian city of the skies ruled by the proclaimed prophet comstock | after going through your baptism you are thrown into a world of religious fanaticism patriotism propaganda ideology and steampunk | i immediately got that bioshock feelingtm of being a misfit in a world where the beliefs of the originator has made the city and its inhabitants gone a bit awry | throughout the game you will be continuously impressed by the sheer spectacle of your surroundings | ken levine and his team has once again managed to create a world which doesn't only impress visually but this time also comments on social issues like racism and religion | these topics are clearly portrayed negatively and this game will be remembered as a standing proof that games surely are as they say art | unfortunately the gameplay is far from as engaging | bioshock infinite has been accused of force feeding you typical first person shooter mechanics and i agree to that point | they add vigors to spice things up supernatural powers equivalent to the plasmids of the earlier titles | to excite things even more you now have sky rails which you can hook onto and ride roller coaster style | this gives some sense of freedom of movement and is a welcome addition to the otherwise way too stale shooter mechanics | the deuteragonist elizaberth has the ability to open up tears ripples into parallel worlds that in practise only works by teleporting various objects and resources into battle | all-in-all i did not feel that these additional combat element alone warrants playing this game and i quickly got tired of the combat sequences | i played the game on the 'hard' difficulty level which felt mostly fine for a more experienced gamer | it does bring with it one annoying problem which was also present in previous titles on the higher difficulty settings | enemies tend to be quite 'bullet spongy' and i did far too often find myself out of both ammunition and salts vigor mana when battling the tougher enemies | when you've emptied your last magazine and thrown all your spells at your opponent after rigorous looting it stops being a matter of skill | there are a fair amount of scripted sequences which in itself can sometimes work for a single player game but when you as a player lose control over booker it hurts your immersion in the game | contrary to previous bioshock titles you now play a fully voiced character in the game | the interplay and dialogue between booker and elizabeth is a core part of the game and this is enhanced through subtle additions like comments and having elizabeth throw you items you might have missed | personally i much prefer the silent protagonist in a first person shooter and every time booker speaks it lessens my feeling of being involved in the world | speaking of the world it cannot be overstated how well crafted and interesting it really is | they have put a lot of effort into various details the levels and even though it might not be that interactive it is still really impressive | i found myself admire various parts of the scenery even though it is essentially just that scenery | technically the game also runs flawlessly on my computer in spite of the good visuals | the ongoing conflict between the rebellious vox populi and the followers of the antagonist comstock is reflected in the levels and is well told through the various places you will visit | i never felt i lost interest in the story which in itself is one of this game's many strong points | i won't spoil any significant parts of it and i instead advise you to experience it yourself | finally i would like to address the elephant in the room | elizabeth as a character is a prime example of the damsel in distress one of the most tired tropes in gaming and this was the aspect of the game that probably bugged me the most | sure there can be some value in this classic type of story but the way it is handled in bioshock infinite is sometimes just plain ridiculous | elizabeth has the power to rip open tears warping space and time itself yet she still appears helpless in front of the hero booker | sure there is a fair amount of character development involved but irrational games could have done so much more with this character had they let her step outside the role of the helpless woman | to summarise i may have bashed this title a bit more than necessary | just praising all the good things would not have made for that interesting of a read and i feel most reviews have already touched upon the better aspects of this title | the biggest strengths of bioshock are its setting and story and if you can bear with the average mechanics and slightly irritating characterisation you will find one of the best titles of |

review_text: bioshock in the sky | irrational games did it again | infinite is just as visually stunning as its predecessors were but this time the story takes you to colombia a floating city in the early th century | you play as booker an agent who's sent to mentioned city to find elizabeth a young girl held hostage for an unknown reason | as opposed to rapture this bioshock lets you see the city in its full glory before all hell breaks loose | the first couple of levels literally make you lost in the environment it's so meticulously and beautifully made that you do not want to believe your own eyes | also in terms of storytelling it is now exciting to be in the middle of the battle between two warring factions: booker witnesses the vox populi who so desperately try to get rid of colombia's finest | in terms of gameplay this bioshock offers nothing new: you have an assortment of weapons at your disposal along with the good-old plasmids | oh wait | in the world of colombia they go by the name of vigors | there are fewer vigors out there and also the weapons do not have special bullets now instead there are upgrades to the both that you can find at various vendors | purchasing them requires a lot of money so the game again appreciates those who are willing to spend some extra time looking for loot in every room and every container found throughout the game | instead of eve you collect salt that restore your magic | there are now secret places in the game where you can find either gear or infusion | the former gives you a boost or special ability e | g | you walk faster or landing from skyline sets nearby enemies on fire while the latter increases your total health salt and armor bar | oh the skyline | your first and only melee weapon is the skyhook which you can also use to ride the skyline this is colombia's very own rail system and lets you quickly go from one place to another | some of the more tense battle sequences require you to use this and you do need to be careful and prepared as enemies will do the same | remember those monsters called big daddy from the first two games | their colombia equivalent is called a handyman | imagine one of these brutes using the skyline and coming after you at great speed | by the way audio diaries are returning as well so if you want to get the related achievement you'd better be exploring everything | there's no map this time | just an arrow helping you showing which direction you're supposed to go | there's no hacking however turrets are returning so your best bet is to use a vigor to make sure they are fighting on your side | there are several themes the story explores and the ending leaves room from interpretation | quite early on you can rescue elizabeth and go together with her and it is interesting to see character development and also getting to know the girl and her story background | elizabeth does not take part in any battles but can help you by opening 'tears'; literally tears in the sky through which machines can come over from a different dimension assisting you or simply equipment is brought through to make sure you do not run out of ammo or medkit | long story short: infinite is a superb sequel | in terms of gameplay this bioshock is a bit more simplified and action-oriented nevertheless the rest of the elements have not changed and remain superb: graphics music and art design | the game offers you only single player experience it's replayability is still high thanks to the various difficulty settings available | i still need to complete burial at sea its story-oriented dlc so i'll keep you guys posted |

review_text: mafia iii is an exercise in tedium | the first couple of hours are decent then the story grinds to a halt as the player is tasked with taking over different rackets and districts of the city | this makes up the large majority of the game and involves you driving between repetitive filler-tier activities that take less time to complete than it does to drive over to them | it's a shame because the handful of properly-designed missions that are in the game are fairly decent | the combat is pretty slick the enemies have good hit reactions to gunfire and the gunfights can be quite fast-paced with the mouse and keyboard controls | most of the gunfights in the game will last about thirty seconds to a minute though considering the repetitive racket-takeover missions make up most of the time | the game has a fair number of bugs too | a few times i'd have to restart missions from a checkpoint because it bugged out and i couldn't progress | if you shoot and kill an enemy near a railing they'll play an animation where they fall over the railing but they'd often freeze at the point where the canned animation was supposed to transition to ragdoll physics so they'd end up suspended in mid-air | if you have police chasing you and you call in the favour to get rid of the cops they'll literally disappear right in front of you | the optimisation is an issue also | in my experience they actually fixed the game up and had it running quite well through post-launch patches but with the latest update the one that introduces racing and car customisation they seem to have reverted all of these optimisations and the game runs like crap again | you can't roll-back to previous builds through steam either so the only way to play the game with good performance now is to download a cracked version of the last build which is absolutely ridiculous | overall on the plus side the game has a nice soundtrack and world; decent characters and acting; and good combat | on the other hand there are only a few good missions hidden amongst hours of absolute tedium; there are bugs; and the latest build screwed up the performance | would only recommend this if you can get it super cheap and you're willing to accept the risk of possibly slipping in to a coma from mind-numbingly boring missions |

| the game's story is a typical revenge story that has the predictable 'i've become the monster i set out to destroy | ' ending | the voice acting and motion capture for cutscenes are generally top notch though occasionally there's a cutscene where the visuals look terrible and the acting feels awkward especially with the priest and his future interviews | his fake crying is unbearable to sit through | i did enjoy getting some closure on the events of mafia concerning vito scarletta and joe barbaro but they felt more like fan service rather than well thought out extensions of their story | i liked the mysterious way mafia ended and the fact that they are suggesting that joe survived kind of ruins the impactful ending of mafia | so yeah the story is decent and definitely the best reason to play mafia but it's nothing extraordinary | the gameplay is where we start running into some serious problems | after a long hour introduction where the timeline jumps around to help explain how the mardi gras heist went down the game suddenly drops off into a highly repetitive crawl throughout the 'open-world' city | i put open world in quotations because the world is beyond empty | there's quite literally nothing to do in new bordeoux aside from the side missions and main story missions | this would be fine if the side missions weren't required in order to unlock story missions | each district in the city requires you to complete repetitive side missions that pretty much always involve you invading an enemy controlled territory and killing a vip inside | you can approach these missions with stealth or combat but neither method makes a difference | there's no reward for playing the game stealthily so there doesn't seem to be a reason to bother most of the time aside from the thrill of sneaking around undetected | you can kill enemies lethally or nonlethally but for some reason you must change a gameplay setting in the game's pause menu whenever you want to switch between these methods | once you complete a bunch of these side missions you are forced to return to that district's friendly ai where you are a treated to a lazy in-engine cutscene that looks like something out of an old tony hawk game and they tell you to go to one of the side mission locations you just cleared to kill an underboss | after killing the underboss you're only halfway done | now yuo need to meet another ally in the same district complete more side missions and then kill another underboss to unlock an actual story mission | now the story missions are a lot of fun most of the time | they are generally large set-pieces like a burning boxing ring or a crashed river boat where you fight your way to one of sal marcano's lieutenants | there's about of these large missions and those alone would have made for a fun experience | but unfortunetly you're stuck grinding away at this lackluster open world and completing side missions for hours | thankfully the side missions can still be fun with the well done ingame economy | i never felt as though i had too much money to spend nor did i feel like mone was too hard to come back | i slowly managed to earn enough money to make upgrades to my arsenal health and vehicles | the melee kills are all awesome and never get old and combat often feels really realistic | the vehicle combat is pretty awkawrd with strange lock-on targetting rather beautiful | the game also causes my gtx ti's fans to get really loud suggesting that the game is forcing my gpu to run way too hot | it's as if they stopped half-way through when making this game | i encountered several bugs that forced me to restart from checkpoint simply because friendly ai failed to perform scripts that allowed me to continue missions | i also had plenty of vehicles spawning ontop of eachother ai acting strangely visual glitches like clouds moving too quickly and really strange massive saturation when inside buildings | so if you're on the fence with your purcahse of review_text: as the old proverb goes revenge is a dish best served cold | but for mafia 's lincoln clay revenge is a dish best served with buckets of blood preferably prepared using a razor sharp combat knife | betrayed and left for dead by the italian mob lincoln subsequently sets out on the warpath hellbent on exacting vengeance upon those who wronged him and destroyed his family | that means dismantling mafia don sal marcano's sprawling criminal empire across the city of new bordeaux one piece at a time | wiping out marcano's criminal rackets is at the heart of mafia 's story as lincoln and his chain-smoking cia insider john donavan set about bringing down enforcers lieutenants and capos before going after the big man himself | however there's more to do beyond simply getting to marcano meaning lincoln requires the help of underbosses cassandra vito scaletta and thomas burke | as you recruit each of these lieutenants you'll gain a variety of perks like an arms dealer a consigliere to collect your cash a hit squad to help out in a fight or vehicle delivery but retaining these means keeping your underbosses happy | as you gain control of each of new bordeaux's rackets you'll assign them to whichever underboss you like before calling a sit down to decide who inherits the entire district | it's up to you whether you favour one or two of your underbosses or take a more diplomatic approach divvying turf up equally between all three | failing to keep an underboss happy however will push them out turning them into an enemy that lincoln will have to deal with | it means the decisions you make during sit downs can have real consequences so you'll need to choose wisely | there are some facets of mafia that you'll need to think about then although for the most part the game's missions are largely variations on the same objective sending you into hostile territory to clear out criminal scumbags | little things like wiretapping junction boxes using fuses also reveals enemy positions other racket locations and collectibles in the region on the mini map making life easier for yourself | an accomplished cover shooter at its core practically every one of the rackets you seize comes from clearing out heavily armed goons whether via stealthy means or through a more gung-ho approach | as such you can expect to be stacking up the bodies murdering enforcers interrogating informants who can be recruited if you'd rather not kill them and inflicting damage to the racket by destroying stashes of drugs chemicals or whatever | it can actually get rather repetitive | thankfully mafia 's shooter mechanics are fantastic as are the rest of the game's open-world systems like the fun driving model that includes a more realistic 'simulation' option that can be toggled on or off or the brutal and gratifying melee combat | by the time you reach the latter stages of mafia you'll be a well-oiled killing machine able to pull off brutal kills and headshots with aplomb | unfortunately mafia is hampered by a whole litany of bugs and other issues most of which are odd visual quirks including some lighting weirdness numerous instances of pop-in nutty physics that send cars flying through the air off the slightest bump character model glitches and regular occurrences where the ai behaves in laughably strange ways | in fact the ai in general can be rather shoddy either seeing you through walls or passing you by completely without noticing you're there | it's a shame because mafia is genuinely enjoyable despite its range of problems | the soundtrack too is utterly stellar stuff delivering the best of s music and bringing its version of a tumultuous new orleans to startling life | the tunes blaring out of the radio from the likes of the rolling stones the beach boys creedence clearwater revival jimi hendrix and others are one of the best bits of mafia | the game's excellent storyline also keeps things ticking along nicely intercut with present day documentary-style sequences and donovan's testimony telling the tale of lincoln clay's vengeful mission from the perspective of the people who were there at the time | it's a great narrative device although there are certain scenes that recount what happened before you've actually had the chance to play out the ensuing scenario | nonetheless mafia 's story is fantastic unflinchingly violent and authentic in its rendition of a turbulent time and place | definitely not for the faint-hearted hangar 's open-world is one that's riddled with rampant racism sex drugs and other criminal activities covered in gritty detail that doesn't pull any punches | where gta revels in sharp satire and humour mafia is a more serious beast not shying away from any of the issues that ran through american culture at the time | from the moment you start the game up there's a statement from hangar saying as much warning that the offensive language and period is shown as it was warts and all | as for the achievements there's a really good spread across all of mafia 's various aspects but there are a couple thrown in there that require a second playthrough | for such an enormous open-world game that seems a bit crappy meaning only the most dedicated will bother to pursue the full g | the majority are devoted to story progress and missions pulling off feats in combat and taking over rackets encouraging you to really get stuck in | a good list overall | a decent open-world game despite its myriad issues and repetitious mission structure mafia excels as a cover shooter and epic crime saga | the problems with the game are outweighed by how enjoyable it is to play with its robust driving and combat and remarkable rendition of s america | look past the bugs and you'll find that mafia is an uncompromisingly violent and well-told drama that also successfully depicts a snapshot of an abhorrent intolerant society |

review_text: mafia iii comes strong out of the gate but then slows down and turns into a marathon grind | many features that you would expect to be in the game are noticably absent some are promised in future patches and while the core gameplay of driving and shooting is satisfying how they are executed in the game is pretty lame | repetitive missions for each district require you to do the same activities before you can challenge the racket bosses which allow you to challenge the capo | the activities are: kill some people destroy some things interrogate some people or steal some things | nothing else | the game does contain some very notable bright spots | the representation of the location a new orleans-clone in louisiana is beautifully depicted and contains the institutional bigotry and racism that were a horrendous hallmark of the era | the characters can be compelling and interesting and the cutscenes are like watching a movie engrossing you in the story's progression | as stated before the shooting and driving mechanics are fun and even though it's a typical cover-based shooter it feels more satisfying as you use your pistol to snipe shot someone yards away kind of like the ai does in other games | the cars handle better than refrigerators on wheels but still lack the finesse of cars with power steering | it's that delicate balance that makes driving enjoyable | also the period soundtrack is amazing although i'm kind of disappointed that jimi hendrix's 'all along the watchtower' is only played during the opening menu | any fan of s music will appreciate the soundtrack in the game | missing features plague the game to keep it from being a truly enjoyable experience | the lack of a home base to store cars change outfits collect earn or even upgrade to spend money on kind of makes the experience pretty hollow | it feels less like you're running a criminal organization and more like you're just running around killing mostly racist people in your linear quest for revenge | k did say that they were going to patch in character customization e | g | the ability to change outfits but that should have already been included from the start | even the fps framerate needed a patch that was released a day after the game came out | why k feels the need to patch these things in at a later time is beyond me | you should not be paying $ dollars for an incomplete product | mafia iii is best enjoyed in short bursts grinding out a racket or two in between other games | i hoped that k wouldn't be patching in features at a later date but it seems like that's what you're going to have to wait for | don't buy it in its current state for full price | wait for the new features to be patched in and then buy it | it can be an enjoyable experience and hopefully once it's complete the game will live up to the potential that was laid down from the beginning | pros: good setting combatdriving is fun decent main storyline when you're not grinding it out good voice acting great soundtrack cons: incredibly stupid driverpedestrian ai enemy ai is pretty shaky repetitive grinding for racketsbossescapos no character customization promised in later stories an action game has had in recent memory | it's nice to play as a black war veteran anti-hero it's a direction that hasn't been taken in many games in the past | it also features a cast of interesting characters at least the ones of any significance to the story | without spoiling too much the high point of the story is definitely the confrontation at the end between clay and the villain; it is realistically one of my favorite moments in any video game | the story isn't perfect it isn't as good as mafia ii's story and is sadly spread too far and few between by an abundance of repetitive and unskippable story missions that don't actually progress the plot | overall though the story and characters are so well written that it has to be a plus | combat: combat is definitely improved in this game over its predecessors | the inclusion of the stealth and brutal execution mechanics are key points which make this a fun game to play | nothing is more satisfying than brutally stabbing a mafiosa repeatedly in the face and then taking out his startled friend with a close range shotgun to the gut that sends him ragdolling back through the air | there is also a great amount of flexibility in the combat tactics you can use in the game | stealth going in guns-a-blazing and any mixture of the two are all valid and useable combat tactics in mafia iii | it also is really rewarding to stealth through one of the racket missions just to sneak up on the man in charge and grab him before he knows what's going on | i do need to make note that the ai is pretty stupid especialy when it comes to the stealth; they will often times look right past you and you can make them throw caution to the wind with a simple whistle to draw them to an area where you can stealth kill them with a simple press of the 'q' key | the flexibility doesn't just come in tactics either | there are a wide range of weapons and explosives to choose from | although it is kind of lame that you have very limited ammo supplies even with the upgrades and additionally can only carry two weapons one small arms and one large arms weapon | i found myself often times dropping the extremely overpriced weapons i had bought purely out of the lack of ammo supply | regardless of these small issues the combat definitely felt improved over mafia ii | exploration: exploring new bordeaux in mafia iii is a lot of fun | each area feels pretty different from any of the others which is crazy considering there are different areas in the city | while exploration isn't very fruitful aside from gathering collectibles see cons it is still enjoyable for explorations sake | if you want to be rewarded tangibly for exploring you may not enjoy the exploration but if you just enjoy virtual site seeing you'll have a good time | soundtrack: the soundtrack is great | while i prefered mafia ii's soundtrack jazz is my jam the use of classic rock songs at specific points of the game was great | also the twangy 'bayou' music that plays during a lot of cutscenes and at the title screen is also great | it does a great job at establishing the setting and the subtle changes depending on actions are both articulate and well executed | i also enjoyed the brief moments where a jazzy song would come on usually while checking out the map but that is just me | intermediate: these are topics that weren't really positives but weren't really negatives either difficulty: i beat the game with relative ease on the hardest difficulty | it seems rather unbalanced to be quite honest | there were certain parts that were extremely difficult and others that were a breeze | these moments were generally outliers though most of the game gave a challenge but not a frustrating one | the way the health and armor worked were also pretty unbalanced and annoying | fully upgraded you have four health bars but getting shot with a shotgun puts you down to about half of a bar and then only that bar will refill unless you use medicine which is extra annoying because the game insists on making medicine hard to come by when you need it and expensive to buy for how often you need to use it for it to be effective | similarly the armor that you spent $ on would disappear after a shotgun shot and pistol shot combined | while it may be helpful in a few situations on the whole it doesn't really do too much | that being said this was only really noticable at certain times | the challenge was generally pretty fair except for two particular instances and definitely made it difficult to try and storm in on an area guns blazing if there were many people there | as i said earlier i beat the game on the hardest difficulty and while that wasn't the most difficult of accomplishments it is certainly better than many modern games i can think of that are just so frustratingly difficult on harder settings | driving: the driving in mafia iii feels pretty meh | a lot of the nuiance that existed in mafia ii was scrapped | speed limiter was totally removed | one improvement though is that while the driving ai is still stupid they look like geniuses compared to the drivers in mafia ii | one really annoying aspect of the driving is that you will often hit something and die but it isn't consistent | sometimes you can get in a head on collision at max speed and live others you hit a twig in a boat going of max speed and die | this is definitely annoying when you make a lot of progress in a mission just to be set back to the last checkpoint for something stupid | i do have to say that driving really fast and with lots of drifting does feel great in this game possibly better than it does in mafia ii | i should mention i was playing with the realistic driving settings on | cons: repetitive: by the end i was pretty much bored of doing the same old racket missions over and over again just to get to the story missions in between | that being said it was worth it to grind through for the story | nevertheless i wish that they could have used more original ideas than the very common go here kill this person or destroy this stuff approach | racket missions also completely lacked story elements | at first they were fun but you have to remember there are rackets to take over | it gets old | also i should mention that all the side missions vito's were actually pretty cool but that was because if you played mafia ii you had a little insider information as to what was going on and you had motivation to do it were ing awful | burke's specifically were terrible | stealing multiple of the same car was so god damn annoying | same thing with the missions you were given to boost rackets | there's only so many times you can steal a boat full of marijuana before it gets old | lack of immersion and customization in mafia ii you had to buy guns and clothes at stores could store and customize cars had to fill up cars with gas and coulld stick up stores | it really sucks to come to mafia iii and see all those things gone | lincoln is stuck in the same outfit the whole game aside from story missions where a specific costume is given for the duration of the mission and while he has stored cars they are all unlocked and have to be called in you don't have a garage that you retrieve them from as previously done | you also buy all your guns and ammo and upgrades from the back of a van that you call in which takes away from the immersion as well | empire bay felt like a real city new bordeaux really didn't | collectables: they have no achievement or even in game benefit for collectors | they're in the way | summary: it plays very much like saints row but more serious and story orientend than goofy and without the immersive factors that mafia ii had previously brought to the series |

playing mafia ii i had high hopes for this game | i heard that the story was great and that the soundtrack was amazing | sadly though it didn't meet my hopes | the game is set in in the fictional city in louisiana called 'new bordeaux' which is basically new orleans | you play as lincoln clay a man who just got back from the war in vietnam | all's well in his life until tragedy strikes and lincoln is out for revenge | now i do admit that the story is pretty darn good | it's probably the best thing going for it | if you've played the previous game you'll also recognize some people | the new characters are also interesting | after the story though things start to get a little average | if you couldn't tell already this game is a third person shooter just like the rest of the series | there are a multitude of guns in your arsenal available to purchase in-game | there's pistols snipers shotguns automatic guns and more | the shooting in this game isn't anything new if you've played any third person shooter you've probably played this one too | being that this is an open world game there is also driving | now the cars in this game look pretty sweet but the driving isn't anything new either | once again if you've played an open world game with cars you've probably played this one too | the one plus with the driving is the radio | the soundtrack has some great hits from the era and do make driving worth it | here's where it drops more | the missions | if you've ever read a review on this game you probably already know this | the missions are all basically the same | you either kill someone or you destroy something | yep | when i first started i was excited about the missions | i do admit that they're pretty fun but they get old fast | it came to the point where i was so lazy that i just got the sniper drove to a vantage point parked the car got out sniped the target and drove off | you can stealth-kill targets which can be fun but it just gets mundane | mission after mission of the same thing | back in mafia missions felt more unique | sure you had your shoot-outs but there were some great missions | now there are some unique missions but most of your time will be spent doing the same interrogation animation times killing one fool several times or smashing up something | one of the goals of the game is to take over the map and that is done by completing missions | when this is done you can assign pieces to your three lieutenants and it's done by holding a meeting | giving pieces of land and completing missions for any of your lieutenants can give you access to new stuff such as weapons | doing the missions though means more of the same stuff | overall i thought this system was fairly cool but it still makes you do the same old missions | another thing to note is the graphics | the in-game graphics are pretty good but sometimes seem a little lack luster | the cut scene graphics though are extremely well done and the whole thing feels like a documentary you'd find on the history channel | also when you're not killing targets or busting up places there's also collectables to be had different cars and clothes to buy | other than the missions though there's not much to do | in the end mafia turned out to be a decent game due to its story music and amazing cut scene graphics | mafia doesn't do a good job in terms of being the next installment to mafia | if you're looking to buy this i'd say wait for it to go down to $ at the very most | $ dollars would be more ideal though and if you're truly looking for that mafia experience stick with the first two games |

review_text: i love you bethesda but you can't be doing that | a relatively good game but i can't bring myself to call it a great game | pros: moddable decent story | decent at best fun gameplay when you're not crashing or freezing combat is fun if you don't run into the bug that causes your game to freeze in vats which ironically i only started encountering after they issued an update to fix this problem settlement mode is kinda fun when you get the hang of it though it's still buggy and very touchy | i would recommend a mod that allows you to slightly place an item within another item's area which helps circumvent the bugginess | who cares if i want a couch to be placed less than inches from a standtable | cons: buggy as all hell | i know what to expect from bethesda in general what with the extremely open environments and choice system but a game-ending crash-to-desktop bug caused me to restart my hour game from scratch and i still ended up catching the same ctd | at least i found a workaround a walkaround technically that took an extra minutes but it basically rendered settlement unusable and was a real pain-in-the | in some other cases quest events fail to trigger and either bug out the quest or force you to use console commands to skip forward--which is at least immersion-breaking | also vats seemed to cause a game freeze % of the time requiring an altf quit conversations are repetitive | instead of a few different options you're set up with basically the exact same conversational setup throughout the game 'more info' 'snarky' 'no' 'nice' diplomacy is a thing of the past--charisma has been nerfed and peaceful routes are almost eliminated | that being said it was very cool in previous games that your skillsstats could open particular conversation routes e | g | high intelligence could allow you to comprehend certain jargon and discuss things in quests and general conversation that an idiot melee character couldn't fathom | this feature is gone | some npc's are extremely annoying | i know there are annoying people in the world but you'd think they could remember that they just held you up to give you the same spiel minutes ago | the goodevil like gta where the hot dog guy will watch you murder cops and then condescendingly sell you a hot dog | almost zero challenge | even on survival mode it's not likely that you will die much | there's a particular fortified settlement that will always respawn its defenses even if you clear everything out | you'd think that you should be able to take control of such a settlement | lastly if this bugs you the game has been in development for years and so has graphics akin to new vegas the previous installment | tl;dr bethesda has wiped out really cool features of their previous game probably to crash-to-desktopiest game i've ever played |

review_text: before anything else i would like to state that most of the things in this review is subjective and thus if you don't like reading people's opinion then this review is probably not for you | with that being said let's dive into the review | fallout one of the more ambitious projects by bethesda to date | and while it has improved in some aspects there's alot of things needed to be improved upon also | pros: gunplay: trust me when i say that the gunplay in this game is alot better than the previous titles although i have problems hitting things while they're moving but it may just only be me | overall it feels alot more smoother and more responsive than ever before | the map: although the map is smaller than skyrim's it's still pretty big and there's alot of things to explore i find myself just getting lost in the landscape | finding places is more a joy than a chore in this game you could be doing a quest when you accidentally find yourself in a ghoul infested millitary base which i quite enjoy | the story: alot of people dislike the story but i actually like it reason being that it invoked genuine emotions from me like when you killed your son i felt really sad or that time when you give arlen glass the holotape of his daughter before the bomb dropped that also made me pretty upset | those are the moments that made me go oh crap | and that's the reason why i liked the story and actually prefer it over new vegas' story | companions: the companions in this game are a joy to be with now they actually interact with you and offer great side commentary which is always fun to hear | and the companion swap dialogue those are amazing | they now feel alot more realistic with their own likes and dislikes | customization: this is a pretty new feature in fallout now you can customize your weapons and armor which is alot of fun | voice acting: the voice acting in this game is superb it really is | every character that i've talked to has emotion and while some people might dislike the voiced main protaganist i actually find it easier to bond with my character due to the fact that heshe speaks | i'm not saying that the voiced protaganist is better i actually like the silent protaganist more but i see the reason bethesda put the main protaganist's voices there | cons: base building: right now at the moment base building feels too clunky and the ui is not at all friendly to the mouse and keyboard | objects like fences don't clip to places where i want them to clip making me very frustrated | difficulty: first off no hardcore mode which is pretty disappointing | but the most disappointing part is that the game is a little too easy after about hours into the game and there's a lack of enemy variety which is a problem with every fallout game i feel they should add more types of enemies like a flying deathclaw that grips you and flings you into the air that's something i would be afraid of | weapon variety: too little weapons | i only hope they will add more with dlcs but that doesn't excuse the amount of weapons there is in the game | the customization helps but more weapons would definitely be appreciated | ai: really really stupid | constantly running into traps jamaica plains is a place of sadness for almost every companion | summary: fallout is one of the more fun games to play this year and although it has it's issues i can't deny that it's an enjoyable game |

review_text: do like rpg games | do you love the fallout franchise | if so you may want to hold off on purchasing fallout | fallout is the next entry in the fallout franchise taking place years after fallout and years after fallout new vegas | while there was a lot of excitement for fallout when it was first announced it has sadly fallen short in almost every capacity | lets start off with the good parts of fallout | graphics: fallout is a beautiful game | it may not have the best graphics out there but even when being played on low settings it is still quite pleasing to the eye | if you add in the fact that you can mod it taking into consideration the games engine you can pull of a level of graphics that would rival the best looking games on the market possibly for quite some time | mods: fallout has a huge amount of mod support with mods being available for console users as well when they get it finished | this enables you to customise your game in virtually any way you see fit without the need to buy a pc in order to do it | music: the music is done very well there are a lot new songs while at the same time some of our favorites from fallout have made a return | sadly though that is about as generous as i can be and it goes down hill from here | for the negatives we will start with the big issues and narrow it down from there | bugs: you would think after doing the fallout franchise for so long they would figure out that they need to get rid of the bugs and glitches before the game is released to the public | there is a reason games go through alpha and beta testing with multiple stages of testing for each and multiple paths until they get things running smoothly | bethesda has not managed to get that down though and much like the launches of previous titles in the series bugs and glitches were rampant in fallout 's launch | while bethesda has patched a few of the glitches and is making effort to smooth out the bugs and improve performance that is all stuff that should have been done before the game is released to the public | skills: one of the big draws at least for me to the rpg genre is the skill systems | picking certain skill sets or classes and running with it | in fallout and new vegas this ment picking between small guns energy weapons melee unarmed and many many other skills | fallout has completely removed the skill system from the game and instead runs with a perk based system similar to that which you would find in fps shooters like call of duty | while some people may enjoy this change and think it was the right decision i for one do not as it no longer feels like an rpg with the system it has currently | impact: fallout has always had a setup in which the players choices had an impact on the game | this could be eliminating a faction and it's members no longer being in the game world | it could also be something as simple as the cut scenes showing a different outcome at the end based on the decisions you made | fallout new vegas took this idea to the next level and made it so just about everything you did impacted the game | from what towns you helped out to what companions you did side quests for or decided to ignore to what factions you decided to help or take out and ending in which of the major factions you sided with in the end if you sided with one at all | all of these decisions were reflected in the end cutscenes discribing to you what kind of impact your decisions had on the game world as a whole | fallout on the other hand is seriously lacking in this department | after having gone through the main story line and played for about hours i don't feel as though i made any impact at all on the game world | yes you choose which factions you help out and which you destroy like in previous games but there is no impact overall | if you choose to eliminate faction a their members with the exception of leadership still exist in the game and there are no cutscenes at the end describing what impact you had | the cutscene they do have is very generic and bland having one scene to fit of the major factions and a second scene to fit for the th faction which doesn't really differ all that much | vats: vats was a huge part of fallout and new vegas | it had its issues yes but it was very important non the less | if you ran into trouble and group of enemys is waiting for you around the corner you just took you enabled vats and took the time to plan out your attacks | in fallout vats is still there although in a different capacity | time no longer comes to a stand still when you activate vats and instead just slows down | while this makes the game sound more challenging at first in practice it just ends up causing more problems then anything else | with the camera freaking out on you trying to keep up and increases number of line of sight issues being among the top of the list | vats really doesn't seem worth it in the long run in fallout | rollplay: the first word in rpg stands for rollplay | it is very difficult to get into a rollplay with your character when you have a voiced protaganist | decide you want to be evil in your playthrough | how evil do you think you can be when your character sounds like a happy peaceful person from | this along with some of the previous mentioned issues kills the rollplay and the replay factors that drive most people to the fallout franchise | ron perlman: i know i know i am kind of nitpicking here but lets face it | ron perlman is the voice of fallout | he is the narrator for every fallout game released so far starting back at fallout | he also has other roles in the fallout universe like playing butch harris in the original fallout | in fallout though he gets a very short part as a tv anchorman at the begining of the game that lasts less then a minute | bethesda you can't do this to us ron perlman is fallout | the final thing i am going to touch on is the shady business practices of bethesda during fallout | when they announced the game orignally they bragged about it's difficulty system and how it ended in survival difficulty | a mode which boasts % damage for the player % damage for the enemys slower hp regen via food and stimpacks and an increased spawn rate for legendary enemys | they also bragged about how if that was not hard enough for you the huge amount of mod support the game would have when the creation kit was released would let you increase the difficulty as much as you would like | this would be similar to skyrim players that used mods like frostfall hunger overhaul hypothermia cloaks of skyrim and many other mods to make skyrim more challenging to them | after months of the game being released though some people starting complaining that the game was not difficult enough and the creation kit was not available yet for them to mod their game to make it more challenging | bethesda's response to this was to do a new game mode called survival which would revamp damage include hunger thirst sleep and other things and overall make the game more difficult | this was fine at first the problem though was in doing so bethesda eliminated the original survival difficulty completely and has told players that liked it to either mod their game to get it back or play on a lower difficulty setting | this is very very bad business practices on behalf of bethesda and a very disappointing move from what was one of my favorite developers | in the end fallout is a very lackluster game that does not feel like a fallout game and instead is more like a post apocalyptic call of duty | i would highly advise you skip this game and spend your money on something else | if you are into rpg games get something like dark souls or one of the many other rpgs out there | if you are into other genres there are a ton of better options for you | tldr: fallout is a very unimpressive game |

review_text: after finally beating the game hours in i can say that fallout is a good game but also a dissapointing one coming from a massive fallout and new vegas fan | bethesda is continuing their tradition of dumbing down their new releases further and further | from morrowind to oblivion to skyrim i don't even consider skyrim an rpg it's an open world action adventure game with rpg elements and they have done a similar thing to fallout | i do think that fallout is an rpg just a very dumbed down one and it honestly didn't feel like one in the first hours | i started getting bored of the game around the hour mark because i felt like i wasn't making an impact in the world enough and everything i did felt meaningless | this was very depressing considering i easily put over hours in and new vegas in multiple playthroughs and was never bored | the same thing happened with oblivion and skyrim | over hours in oblivion and i was done with skyrim in hours | this is all mainly because the games are dumbed down massively making them less engaging for me | after beating the game i do not see myself putting more hours into it exploring the rest of the world like i was planning | maybe i will in future but not anytime soon i wanna move on to something else | when i got to the second half of the main story the game picked up big time and it started giving you meaningful choices that effects the world | the game is missing the karma system and you can't really be evil in this game either | i think those additions would have made the game much better | the shooting is not clunky anymore it feels fluid and the ai is better then the previous games but on the other hand i found no reason to use vats at all on the pc because the aiming is so smooth with the mouse and keyboard | however on console you will still probably use it cause aiming on controller is awkward | in the other games i was using vats all the time i rarely shot a bullet without it because the shooting was so clunky but that was the charm of the game because if i wanted to play a shooting game i would go play the hundreds of them out there on the market and thats not why i play fallout and sadly fallout fits into that category of shooters | this opinion is very personal and subjective and its totally ok if you disagree because the shooting itself is better in this game and i understand if you like it more because of that | the weaponsarmor don't break in this game i simply dont get why they did this other than to appeal the game more to casuals and further dumb down the game i really like the crafting i think its a great addition from building settlements to upgrading weapons and armour its very well done | i love how looting is in real time and you don't have to go into a menu anymore to pick something up it's the best improvment the game has made for me | i do like the addition of your character speaking however the negative is you cannot role play as yourself anymore because of the voice and the character is speaking for you rather than you speaking for yourself | i played as a female because i think it fits the story better and the voice actress plays jack from mass effect which was the big appeal for me | i think the voice actress did a good job for what she was given because i think the writing and the dialogue in this game is awful | the dialouge wheel is horrendous % of the time the options are either 'what | ' 'yes' 'no' 'sarcastic' | very bad | the story is better then fallout 's and it holds up pretty well with new vegas too its just the little things that makes the other fallout games better to me | the side missions and the faction missions in the other fallouts were much more interesting imo as well as the locations you were visiting | boston was not as interesting as dc or the mojave either | the pc optimisation isn't very good | the ui is awful you can easily tell its a console port and there are frame drops even on high end pc's | if you dont have a ssd drive or alot of free memory on your pc the loading times are horrendous | the game looks pretty awful in the boston ruins but looks great in the wasteland its very inconsistent visually | i can make this review go on forever but i should wrap things up | i can still recommend this game | it's a good game it's just a bad fallout game | good

scrolls series progressive drifting from being a pure rpg like morrowind to more of an fps adventure game with rpg elements like skyrim; fallout feels much more like a shooter than an rpg | as you review_text: i once heard a story about a man who tired of the 'perfect temperature' conflict with his wife rigged the heating and cooling in his house so that it was controlled not by the thermostat never discovered the truth until her husband died and her children discovered the calculator | fallout makes me feel like that wife | you're presented with an enormous world full of detail and what seems to be a thousand different little things you can do--settlement-building crafting dialogue options to name a few--but after a dozen hours or so you realize that for the most part they're simply fancy buttons on the thermostat that really don't change your progression through the game | settlements offer little more than a pretty place to look at if you're tired of shooting baddies in the | when you're sitting on doses of radaway you don't even think twice before wading into radiation to check something out | the hacking minigame loses its appeal after your first failure when you or rpg flair | don't like your initial s | p | e | c | i | a | l | stat limitations | don't worry you can wear magic clothes take drugs or even purchase permanent stat upgrades to become a veritable superman who can do anything | it's as if bethesda simply wants you to be happy with the enormous detailed setting in which fallout takes place | and sadly even the setting fails after a time | the first impression of this game is that it's a decade old | the engine is god-awful | characters look like plastic mannequins shoddy textures pop in and out body animations are robotic and facial like a glimpse back in time to the s as a whole which is exactly as it should be; the albums are allegedly the only musical survivors of the s apocalypse | rather than creating another thoughtful the toilet | there is little strategy in this game skills are gone and with it the careful planning of making specialized character builds | there is no level cap you can get all the perks in the game with one character and you can get points into each special stat | bethesda has choosen not to go along with the damage threshold system featured in new vegas and has gone back to the arguably inferior damage resistance system meaning that a gun that shoots ten thousand bb pellets a minute will do more damage against an enemy wearing power armor than a high calliber rifle so there is generally no reason to go with anything but the weapon with the highest damage per second | weapons and armor no longer need to be repaired with the exception of power armor meaning that having multiples of the same weapon or armor in your inventory is uneeded weight for the most part once you have a weapon or armor you will never need another of the same kind | the new dialog system is uttterly terrible you can only guess what your character will say from a few words for each option which you only get of so quick saving during dialog is advisable as it isn't uncommon for you to expect your character to say one thing and then totally say the opposite | the pc version of this game feels as though it has been very neglected as if it were some retaliation to the paid mods fiasco for skyrim | the promise of an uncapped frame rate seems to have been a flat out lie as the game's actual speed is directly tied to it's framerate and attempts to uncap the frame rate in the config files makes the game unstable | this is absolutely unacceptable for a aaa game in | the game also still runs on the same engine bethesda has used since oblivion but of course a very updated version review_text: welcome to the post-apocalyptic wonderland of beautiful metropolitan boston ma fallout | as per tradition bethesda's rpg recipe remains unchanged: open world quests levels and skills sly and witty humorous remarks all decorated in the current coat of paint they have on hand at the time; medieval fairy tale land or post-apocalyptia all wrapped in an engine that's easy to mod | it's buggy it's an unjustifiable resource hog and the story isn't the best out there but all that is quickly forgotten once you've sprayed your first opponents brain across the room in such a wonderfully gory manner that even the old colosseum minded romans would applaud | so nuclear war has hit and you being the smart cookie that you are signed up for a full suite in a cryogenically frozen coffin safe from outside radiation | fast forward a couple hundred years and your son in stolen from you your significant other killed before your eyes and you're out for revenge | the first thing you are introduced to in fallout is settlement creation | a new feature in bethesda games you are now able to collect resources from the commonwealth build houses and furniture recruit people to live and work there and sustain a healthy settlement amidst the ruins of a post nuclear world | its all very wonderful really playing sims when you should be doing better things | i spent a great deal of time building the perfect village building houses placing farms electric systems water pumps walls defenses and managing my settlers while waiting for the next idiot to send a squad of attackers my way | needless to say my defense turrets got the job done before i could taste the blood of battle | the combat system is quite comprehensive yet as simple as firing a gun | all weapons are modable as is armor and allow you to upgrade them with whatever you want providing you have the right skill or perk leveled up of course | the weapons feel right and very organic recoil and range feel spot on and handle as expected | my favorite is the rifle of course with its long range high stopping power and very satisfying head shot head explosions | v | a | t | s | makes a return and aids in killing those oh so hard to hit targets | just pick the body part you want to hit press a button and enjoy the carnage | quite prevalent seems to be the power armor a strong suit of armor requiring uncommon to find power cores that make you a bit tougher and cooler | you can paint and mod it of course though it does require repairs every few battles depending on how much hits you take | i didn't wear it that much as it completely changes the hud and requires parts maintenance | there are four main factions for whom you will be doing your bidding in the commonwealth | the boy scout minutemen aim to make the world a better place for humans and the like the brotherhood of steel who hate everything non human specifically synths the railroad who like trains want to free synthetic life and the synth makers themselves the institute the bringers of technology and the new hope for underground life | the story throws you into interactions with all of them and due to your devilish good looks make you the go to guy for every peanut bag they need opened | finally you are given the option on whom you want to side with which will change certain quest paths but disappointingly not alter the ending by much | gameplay allows you to rely on however you want to approach certain situations | going in guns blazing or armed only with your fists seem to be the popular way of doing things sneaking is always an option though it's rarely viable if you don't have the right perks | talking your way out of certain sticky situations is still a possibility sometimes but again only if you have the correct perks | perks do make the character and although there is no need to carefully plan them they will determine your play style for the duration of your playthrough | the level cap is set at a rather high number though so in theory you could get most of the perks you wanted | technically speaking the game is a mess | bugs spawn a plenty as with any bethesda game but do not prove to be game breaking | hardware requirements seem drastically too high compared to what the final product looks like | it does seem like a month more time on the optimization table would rid any hindrance of performance issues | on less than recommended specs i did notice some very unreasonable frame drops in some areas of the game and zooming in on some scopes tanked it down to the point that i steered clear of scoped weapon mods altogether | i thought that it was unjustifiable too as the game does not look all that amazing to warrant such high hardware taxation | some d models looked more like they were put together with clay and some textures are far away from belonging in a game however to some degree this does help with loading times | the developers do make good use of special effects and lighting as moonlit scenes of low fog in forest areas look quite peaceful | rain feels like it washes all your radiation cares away and radiation storms make you want to just hide under the covers with on e of your faithful companions | so i can't really say the game looks ugly as the style in which is presented in fits so well with everything else | aided by the wonderful score composition which is so good it had me shut the in game radio off the game just feels amazing and you can't be bothered to care about its imperfections | it took me about hours to complete the game % achievements but that's really a huge understatement of how much content it provides as i probably missed a fair amount of content and quests | it's an open world game and it's not a boring world by any stretch | everything you find could potentially amuse you in some way or another | humorous anecdotes await those who only need to seek them | the story is far from spectacular and it's technically not the most stable game but that doesn't mater | from building villages whatever kind of combat you desire looting or just exploring the neat and the strange this game is extremely fun |
